name: Coldframe Quickshift Night Operative Set
description: Designed for runners who do most of their work between midnight and four in the morning, this set prioritizes silence, thermal management, and the fastest possible identity change. The outer shell is a slim-cut insulated jacket in deep navy with a charcoal grey reverse — both sides treated with noise-dampening microfiber on all moving surfaces, so zippers, velcro, and seam edges make no sound when the wearer is in motion. The jacket converts side-out to side-in in under eight seconds with practiced hands, changing the visible silhouette and color entirely. Interior pockets include a shaped holster channel on each side of the chest, a flat document sleeve along the lower back, and a battery pack housing at the right hip with a dual-routing conduit that feeds both forearm and thigh-level chrome simultaneously. The hood deploys from a collar roll and includes a thin balaclava layer sewn into the inner hood — pull it down and the face coverage deploys without removing the jacket. Beneath, a black long-sleeve thermal shirt with bioluminescence-blocking outer treatment — for runners with bioluminescent geneware, the shirt's outer layer suppresses the glow entirely when buttoned to the collar. Bottoms are close-fit dark olive tech trousers with a thigh-holster integration on the right leg, a digitigrade gusset option built into the seat and thigh for gene-modified runners, and silent-edge hem cuffs that don't rasp on surfaces when crawling. Footwear is a matte black low-boot with memory-foam split sole, ankle wrap closure with no metallic hardware, and a recessed toe cap.
functionality: Eight-second full reversal for identity shift, noise-dampening all-surface treatment, dual chest holster channels, document sleeve at lower back, dual-routing battery conduit for forearm and thigh chrome, deployable hood balaclava, bioluminescence-suppressing shirt treatment, thigh holster integration, digitigrade gusset accommodation, silent-edge hem cuffs, no-metal-hardware ankle closure
what_it_says: Navy is not black — and that distinction is intentional. Black reads as trying too hard; navy reads as someone who works nights and dresses practically. The quality of the silence this outfit produces is its real signature — no rustle, no clink, no rasp. Runners who wear this are telling other professionals that they take craft seriously. The bioluminescence suppression is a courtesy to gene-modified wearers who need to work dark — and a signal that whoever made this thought of everything.
worn_by: gene-modified runners with bioluminescent traits who work dark environments
runners with both upper and lower body chrome requiring simultaneous power routing
operatives who change cover identity mid-job routinely
manufacturer: Coldframe — anonymous street label, believed to be a single fabricator operating out of a Tier 2 basement workshop in the Circuit District
story_hooks: A runner is mid-reversal in a stairwell when footsteps approach from above — they complete the flip in six seconds but the balaclava layer snags, leaving it half-deployed. They have to hold a conversation with a building security guard with the balaclava bunched around their chin, explaining it as a scarf.

The bioluminescence-suppression treatment on the shirt has started to degrade in patches — a runner with chest-level bioluminescent geneware is leaking faint light through the fabric at the collar. On a night job, a guard notices what looks like a faint pulse of light from the runner's neck.

Another operative shows up to the same job site wearing the same Coldframe set in the reversal color. Both of them freeze. Someone hired two crews for the same job — or one of them is not who they say they are.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purposeful silhouette designed for nocturnal infiltration. The reversible jacket dominates — slim and tailored, hitting mid-hip with a structured collar that conceals a deployable hood. Layered beneath is a fitted thermal base. The trousers are equally austere: narrow through the hip and thigh, with subtle reinforcement panels and integrated hardware channels that suggest function over form. The boots are minimalist and predatory. Overall impression: a ghost waiting to move.
physical_description.fit: Compression-adjacent without restriction. The jacket is slim but allows movement; the thermal underneath creates a second skin. Trousers are close-fit with strategic gussets for modified physiology. Everything moves with the wearer, nothing flaps or catches. Designed for maximum range of motion and minimum acoustic signature.
physical_description.primary_material: Ballistic synth-weave outer (navy/charcoal reversible), noise-dampening microfiber on all articulation points, bioluminescence-blocking bio-treated inner layer on thermal shirt, memory-foam sole, treated leather reinforcement panels
physical_description.texture: Smooth outer shell with barely-perceptible texture; seams are flat and sealed. Microfiber on zippers and edges feels almost slick to the touch. The thermal base has a soft, compressive feel. Heel-to-toe memory foam yields without sound.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: deep navy blue and charcoal grey (reversible). Secondary: matte black (thermal layer, trousers, boots). Accents: dark olive on trousers. No logos, no reflective elements, no visible stitching in high-contrast colors.
physical_description.closures: Silent-spec closures throughout: magnetic snaps and friction-fit systems on the jacket, no traditional zippers or velcro (replaced with microfiber-lined mechanical slides). Ankle wrap on boots uses reinforced friction straps, no buckles or metal hardware. Hood deploys via internal collar mechanism.
distinctive_features: Reversible jacket design — full color/silhouette change in under eight seconds
Integrated balaclava hood that deploys from collar roll without removing jacket
Chest-mounted holster channels (left and right) shaped for chrome handguns
Flat document sleeve running along lower back interior
Hip-mounted battery pack housing with dual-routing conduit for chrome limb power
Bioluminescence-blocking outer treatment on thermal shirt — suppresses geneware glow when buttoned
Digitigrade gusset option in seat and thighs (for gene-modified runners)
Silent-edge hem cuffs that produce no rasp on surfaces
Recessed toe cap on boots — no protruding hardware
All microfiber-lined articulation points — zippers, seam edges, closures are acoustically inert
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional with Tier 2 craftsmanship touches. Street-made, not corporate, but built with precision that suggests either a highly skilled single fabricator or a very small crew. The price point and anonymity place it in the working-class professional market — runners, fixers, night-shift operatives who can afford custom gear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by nocturnal professionals: corporate infiltrators, data runners, black-market couriers, chrome-augmented operatives working off-books. The design philosophy screams 'I work in the dark and I don't want to be heard or remembered.' Wearing this says: I have skills, I have chrome, I have work that doesn't happen in daylight, and I can afford anonymity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; worn pieces show localized creasing at elbows, knees, and collar from repeated deployment cycles, but never torn or visibly damaged. Owners maintain these meticulously — a broken seam could mean death. After heavy use, the microfiber edges may show slight wear, and the memory foam sole develops subtle compression marks, but the silence signature remains intact.

image_prompt: Neo-noir fashion photography: sleek androgenous model or dark mannequin draped in a reversible navy-to-charcoal slim insulated jacket, chest harnesses barely visible beneath, deployable hood coiled at collar. Fitted black thermal long-sleeve visible at neckline. Close-fit olive tech trousers with integrated thigh-holster channel. Matte black memory-foam boots with recessed toe caps. Half the frame shows the wearer mid-motion, jacket beginning to flip — the grey reverse just becoming visible. Moody tungsten and cool blue ambient lighting, hard shadows. Urban backdrop: rain-slicked alley, abandoned warehouse corner, or neon-edged Circuit District rooftop. Zero reflective surfaces, zero color pop — everything designed to dissolve into shadow. Cinematic, predatory, silent. --ar 2:3 --v 6
